A1.justification: Both PDFs describe L2RSI, and all supplied pages, figures, tables and equations are readable. However, both identify themselves as extracts: Section 3 contains unresolved references instead of detailed methodology, and neither PDF contains appendices. This limits comparison of the underlying algorithms.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization experiments on XA-L&RSI and cross-scene evaluation on Oxford-L&RSI in Table 2 and Figure 1.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and additional comparisons of refinement variants in Table 3, alongside Figure 1.

M1.justification: Both versions describe semantic alignment and Gaussian-mixture temporal refinement. v2 changes the stated orientation source to a magnetometer and replaces DGMM-ProP terminology with STPE particle aggregation. The missing methodology prevents determining whether the refinement procedure changed substantively or was renamed and explained more fully.

E1.justification: The same XA-L&RSI regions and two Oxford trajectories remain. The evaluated sensing scenario changes from GPS/INS-provided orientation to noisy magnetometer orientation, including simulated noise on Oxford; geographic and localization-task coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 retains GeoDTR, Sample4Geo and FRGeo, while adding SuperGlobal reranking and classical particle filtering as alternative refinements. This substantially expands comparison of the central refinement contribution beyond v1's retrieval-network comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported orientation conditions change to magnetometer measurements with average error below 10 degrees on XA and simulated noise within ±15 degrees on Oxford. The main comparison table replaces Recall@5 with Recall@10, retaining Recall@1 and the 30 m correctness threshold. The new particle-filter comparison specifies 120 initial particles.

E4.justification: v2 adds an unrefined L2RSI ablation and comparisons among refinement strategies, absent from the supplied v1. These directly examine the contribution of temporal refinement: on Test Set-G, Recall@1 is 22.62% without STPE, 47.85% with particle filtering and 83.27% with STPE.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's sensor-error and injected-noise specifications describe experimental inputs rather than uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Full-model Recall@1 on Test Set-G changes from 95.08% in v1 Table 2 to 83.27% in v2 Table 3; Oxford values change from 68.75%/69.05% to 42.29%/43.77%. Most baseline scores also change, and new variant results are reported. These are revised outcomes under changed orientation conditions, not established same-setting performance losses.

T1.justification: Equation (1) and the retrieval definitions remain unchanged. Section 2 replaces the explicit assumption of known absolute orientation obtained through GPS/INS with a noisy magnetometer measurement, constituting a limited change to the formal input assumption. Neither extract supplies proofs or detailed derivations.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims operation using only LiDAR and a magnetometer, without GPS or IMU, in its introduction and new Table 1. This materially changes the operational scope relative to v1's GPS/INS heading premise. The abstract also revises the headline 100 km2 Recall@1 claim from 95.08% to 83.27%, while retaining the large-scale localization contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing particle-filter weakness to particle decay and reinitialization disrupting sequence information, and contrasts this with STPE aggregation. Its conclusion newly identifies magnetometer dependence as a limitation to address. The existing qualification that Oxford results are insufficient for deployment remains.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands previously sparse dataset-construction details: 0.5 m imagery resolution, 60 m crops at 40 m intervals, road-based filtering, 5 m LiDAR submap spacing, 60 m BEV images and a three-year acquisition gap. It also specifies sensor noise, particle count and GPU memory. Previously unstated crop and sampling details establish improved disclosure, not necessarily changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shao et al.'s Global Features Are All You Need for Image Retrieval and Reranking to support the SuperGlobal comparison. The other fourteen cited works remain, and the broader positioning against prior cross-view localization research is retained.

P1.justification: The five main sections remain in the same order. v2 expands the introduction around two explicit challenges, consolidates four contribution bullets into three, adds explanatory passages and changes DGMM-ProP terminology to STPE. These are localized revisions rather than a document-wide restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conditions/tasks table, transposes and expands the performance table into a full-width display, and rescales Figure 1's recall axis. The dataset map and overall two-column presentation remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the supplied paper through more reproducible data and sensor specifications and comparisons that better isolate the contribution of temporal refinement. Detailed methodology remains unavailable, and a new reporting inconsistency limits the gains: Section 4.4.1 claims Oxford Recall@10 exceeds 60% on both trajectories, whereas Table 3 reports 59.41% and 62.76%. Lower headline scores under changed sensing conditions do not themselves establish deterioration.
